title: Median of a piecewise PDF
source: S2 Ch4 theory S2-4.2 Quick check 4 (piecewise: area 1/3 then height 1/3, median 2.5)
stem: The continuous random variable \(X\) has probability density function \(\mathrm{f}(x)=\dfrac{2x}{{den|int}}\) for \(0\le x\le{c|int}\), \(\mathrm{f}(x)=\dfrac13\) for \({c|int}\le x\le{R|int}\), and \(\mathrm{f}(x)=0\) otherwise. Find the median of \(X\).

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Area on \(0\le x\le{c|int}\): \(\displaystyle\int_0^{{c|int}}\dfrac{2x}{{den|int}}\,\mathrm{d}x=\dfrac13\lt \dfrac12\), so the median is in the second piece.
steps.note: Identify the correct piece.

steps.name: A1ok
steps.text_tex: First-piece area \(=\dfrac13\lt \dfrac12\), so the median is in the second piece.
steps.note: Identify the correct piece.

steps.name: I
steps.note: Remaining area 1/6 at height 1/3.

steps.name: M
steps.note: Correct median.

title: Linear PDF on [1, 2]: constant and median

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (Cambridge International Examinations 2015).

stem:
A random variable \(X\) has probability density function given by
\(\mathrm{f}(x)=\begin{cases}k(3-x) & 1\leqslant x\leqslant 2,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}\)
where \(k\) is a constant.

steps.name: m
steps.note: MS: M1 attempt ∫f(x)=1, ignore limits, or k(h1+h2)/2=1.

steps.name: I
steps.note: MS: A1 correct integration and limits, or k(2+1)/2=1.

steps.name: k
steps.note: MS: A1 no errors seen (answer given).

steps.name: m1
steps.note: MS: M1* attempt ∫f(x)=0.5, ignore limits, or use of area of a trapezium. Equivalent: integral from m to 2.

steps.name: lim
steps.note: MS: dep M1* substitution of correct limits into their integral, or trapezium using 1 and m (or m and 2).

steps.name: qe
steps.note: MS: A1 any correct 3-term quadratic = 0, or (m−3)²=2.5.

steps.name: med
steps.note: MS: A1 m=1.42 (3 s.f.) or (6−√10)/2 (oe); single correct answer (the root in [1,2]).

title: Quadratic PDF: constant, median, and a probability

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (Cambridge International Examinations 2015). Part (ii) includes a sketch, which cannot be auto-marked; that part is manual / self-marked.

stem:
The probability density function of the random variable \(X\) is given by
\(\mathrm{f}(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{3}{4}x(c-x) & 0\leqslant x\leqslant c,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}\)
where \(c\) is a constant.

steps.name: m
steps.note: MS: M1 attempt to integrate f(x) and = 1. Ignore limits.

steps.name: I
steps.note: MS: A1 correct integration and limits (condone inserting c=2).

steps.name: c
steps.note: MS: A1 no errors seen (answer given).

parts.stem: Sketch the graph of \(y=\mathrm{f}(x)\) and state the median of \(X\).

answer.official: median = 1; sketch an inverted parabola through (0,0) and (2,0), zero elsewhere

steps.name: sk1
steps.text_tex: The graph is an inverted parabola.
steps.note: MS: B1 inverted parabola. The sketch is self-marked.

steps.name: sk2
steps.text_tex: It passes through \((0,0)\) and \((2,0)\) and is zero elsewhere (it must not extend beyond \([0,2]\)).
steps.note: MS: B1 through (0,0) and (2,0) and zero elsewhere; must not extend beyond [0,2].

steps.name: med
steps.note: MS: B1 median = 1.

steps.name: m
steps.note: MS: M1 attempt to integrate f(x); ignore limits.

steps.name: I
steps.note: MS: A1 correct integration, ignore limits.

steps.name: lim
steps.note: MS: B1 use of correct limits [0,1.5] or 1−[1.5,2].

parts.stem: Hence write down the value of \(\mathrm{P}(0.5\lt X\lt 1)\).

steps.name: h
steps.note: MS: B1f [1] ft their (iii). For use of symmetry. Note: if they do not use ‘hence’ and start again, B1 for cwo.
